attempts.summary: On node1, installed libpam-pwquality (which auto-wires pam_pwquality.so into /etc/pam.d/common-password) and set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf, enforcing new passwords be at least 12 characters with at least 3 character classes. Verified via live passwd attempts by an unprivileged test user: passwords under 12 chars and passwords with <3 classes were both rejected with explicit BAD PASSWORD messages, while a compliant 15-char, 4-class password was accepted. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id/uptime and policy state, issued `shutdown -r now` in background so the ack returned first, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just an elapsed-time or service-restart), and re-verified the pwquality config, PAM hook, and package were intact post-reboot, then re-ran the live weak/strong password test to confirm the policy is still enforced. Test users created for verification were deleted afterward, leaving no residual state changes.
